concept.name: Layer 2
concept.definition: A layer 2 (L2) is a protocol built on top of a layer-1 blockchain that handles transactions off the base chain to increase speed and throughput while deriving its security from the L1's consensus — chiefly via rollups, state channels, or related constructions.
concept.intuition: An L2 is an express lane that does the fast driving elsewhere but files the paperwork at the L1 courthouse, so the L1's security still backs every transaction.
concept.mechanics: Users transact on the L2 (usually via an operator called a sequencer); the L2 batches transactions and posts compressed data and/or proofs to L1 contracts. Rollups (optimistic or zero-knowledge) anchor data availability and dispute resolution on the L1; true L2s can be exited trustlessly using the on-chain data, unlike sidechains.
concept.failure_modes: Most L2s run a single centralized sequencer that can censor or reorder transactions and is a liveness single point of failure; bridge contracts holding L1 escrow are high-value exploit targets.
concept.misconceptions: Not everything marketed as L2 inherits L1 security — sidechains and validiums secure their own data and are weaker. Cheap L2 fees do not mean the L2 is trustless; sequencer centralization is the norm today.
concept.example: On Arbitrum (an optimistic rollup), a token swap costs a few cents instead of several dollars on Ethereum; the batch containing it is posted to Ethereum, and withdrawals to L1 finalize after a ~7-day challenge window unless a fast-exit liquidity provider is used.
